articles.title: What is it like to work when your co-workers are AI agents?
articles.summary: Using AI for roles from executive assistants to chiefs of staff, companies are boasting about doing more with less, creating tension with their human workers. On an average workday, Dhruv Amin chats with dozens of colleagues to get things done at his AI startup Anything.
body: But none of these co-workers are people. They’re artificial intelligence agents, software that handles tasks without human intervention. Anything is one of several startups building them, and betting on a future where workplaces will increasingly turn over their sales, marketing, coding and other tasks to semi-autonomous AI. At Anything, there are 15 human employees and roughly 150 agents – a ratio that Amin believes will soon be the norm.
“I think in a year, every company will have more AI co-workers than human co-workers,” he said.

In the San Francisco tech scene, agents have quickly become a new status symbol, showing that a company can do more with less, several startup employees said. It’s common for workers to brag about how well their agents can handle common office drudgery like answering emails or help with essential business operations such as giving sales pitches.

But agents are also creating tension. They are alienating customers and colleagues who seek human interaction, eliminating roles and forcing employees to become overnight managers of the bots that often make mistakes.

articles.title: ‘Algorithms make everything predictable’: why the CD is making a comeback
articles.summary: As John Lewis reports a 96% rise in searches for CD players, music fans share their reasons for ditching streaming. CDs appear to be having a resurgence. John Lewis said searches for CD players are up 96% since July, while another report on trends in music and film this year found that CD sales are…
body: With this in mind, we asked music fans why they favour discs over other formats, and if it is a new preference or a lifetime habit.

Andrew Wales, 67, from London, owns “well over 10,000” CDs. “My wife’s very considerate,” he says over the phone. “There’s quite a few in this room where I’m speaking.” They have also spilt into the next bedroom and into the corridor.

“I don’t need Spotify,” says Wales. “The fact is, I like listening to music and I have always preferred owning it in a physical form. The [size of the] CD format allows me to own the number I own despite living in a two-bedroom flat and not a country mansion, so that’s another bonus.”

Much of the classical music Wales buys and listens to is available only on CD. “I bought my first CD in 1991 – John Scofield, Meant to Be – around the same time that I bought my first CD player. LPs were becoming increasingly shoddy, both in terms of pressing and presentation, and their limitations meant that often or not songs or tracks were included on the CD release, but not on LP. There are still cases where that happens today.”

articles.title: Tiny basement turned ‘exuberant’ apartment wins interior prize at Australia’s National Architecture awards
articles.summary: With a footprint of less than 40 sq metres, the Melbourne project required careful planning – and some spatial trickery. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email. Last week on a balmy spring evening, Ronnen Goren and his partner had dinner in a small pavilion on their terrace for the first time.
body: This domestic scene took place in a semi-subterranean former laundry in inner Melbourne – a space of less than 40 sq metres that was renovated at the end of 2024. On 29 October, the “exuberant” reimagining of the damp basement space in Toorak, on the grounds of the heritage-listed Quamby apartment complex, received the Emil Sodersten award for interior architecture at Australia’s National Architecture awards.

Originally designed as a service space by the acclaimed Australian architect Roy Grounds in 1941, its rebirth was overseen by Timothy Hill of Partners Hill. The project, titled Studio8, has transformed a poorly executed 1970s apartment conversion into an ambient retreat that belies its tiny footprint.

In 2022, despite the apartment’s “grim” condition, Goren says he and his partner were drawn to its “amazing location” and its “heritage and provenance”, not to mention the north-facing courtyard that’s almost bigger than the apartment. They lived in it as it was for about 18 months, “just imagining what it could be”.
That’s where Hill – whose interest in converting secondary spaces into quality housing stock dates back to his university days – came in.

articles.title: Food-Themed Fashion Is Starting to Feel Gluttonous
articles.summary: There was a time, not too long ago, when a purse shaped like a baguette felt like a thrilling — even subversive — novelty. Now, we hardly bat an eye when we see that Moschino has made a trompe l’oeil celery purse, or that Big Bud Press is making a hot-dog-and-pretzel-print jumpsuit in collaboration…
body: If you buy something from a link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Fashion has long found inspiration from the culinary world, but the influx of food-fueled prints, graphics, and trompe l’oeil accessories that picked up steam during the pandemic have now reached a cultural tipping point.

The then-emerging brand made food a central theme of its vision: Its cake-topped aviator caps, Ferrero Rocher heels, and beeswax-sculpted cheese hats — hyperrealistic, absurdist food designs capable of achieving instant social media virality. Prior to working in fashion, Puppets designer Carly Mark was working as an artist whose pieces revolved around candies and snacks. As she told Business of Fashion in 2023, the Puppets universe felt like the ideal pairing given what she considers food and fashion’s motivators: pleasure and money.

articles.title: Behind the scenes at the scream park: fear, fainting, clowns – and ‘code brown’
articles.summary: At Norfolk’s ‘premier scare attraction’ there are ghouls, chainsaws, satanic cults and a haunted hospital. But what goes on behind the scenes? ‘We always say to the scare actors, you’re going to think the boys will be the worst.
body: This is part of the workplace induction at PrimEvil, one of many immersive “scream parks” that pop up across the UK in the lead up to Halloween. For about £40 a ticket, groups of all ages spend the night roaming themed attractions and being terrorised by actors and special effects. Though the risks are minimal, the spikes in heart rate are very real.

For Francis and the rest of the team, PrimEvil is months in the making. The nightly production involves more than 100 actors and dozens of crew, spread across six themed attractions, each drawing from familiar horror tropes – the scary clowns at the Circus of Terror, the cannibalistic trailer-dwellers over at Route 666, the satanic cult of The Offering. The winding routes are designed to disorient you with strobe lights, smoke machines, mirrored walls, hidden doors, false exits and unstable floors. But it’s down to the performers to bring the nightmare to life.

articles.title: The Best Top-Handle Bags Will Polish Up Any Look
articles.summary: Shop our edit of the best top-handle bags—this structured style comes in a variety of sizes, from party purses to large totes—from Coach, The Row & more.
body: No handbag trend was more dominant on the fall 2026 runways than the top-handle. Designers across the fashion capitals sent models down the catwalk carrying purses by one or two short straps, putting the handheld style firmly back in the spotlight. But if the phrase “top handle” still conjures images of overly prim bags that look plucked from another era, this season’s assortment will have you reconsidering the once-retro category.

Rather than adhering to one specific aesthetic, the latest crop of top-handle handbags runs the gamut. There are elongated east-west shapes that tap into one of the year’s biggest accessory trends, alongside more relaxed, but equally of-the-moment slouchy options. Practical shoppers have plenty to choose from, too, thanks to roomy totes and bucket bags that work just as well for a morning work commute as they do for a weekend outing. And, of course, there are still the ladylike versions we’ve long associated with the top handle: refined envelope styles and nostalgic kiss-lock purses that can make even jeans and a sweater look elegant.

articles.title: How to Brighten Skin, According to Skin Experts
articles.summary: Brightening dull skin is easy once you identify the cause of it. Here, board-certified dermatologist Shauna Higgins and esthetician Raquel Medina-Cleghorn break down all you need to know to boost your natural radiance.
body: The secret to that enviable glowing complexion might not be as elusive as you might think. Brightening dull-looking skin really only requires figuring out what is causing it and making a few tweaks in your skin routine (and maybe a visit to your favorite esthetician for a peel or laser, but more on that later).

Dull skin isn’t inherently bad or dangerous, but no one wants to look dry and tired. So whether you want ultimate shine with that glass skin look or just a natural-looking boost in radiance, consider this your ultimate guide to brightening dull skin.

Many things can cause a dull complexion. Raquel Medina-Cleghorn, esthetician and founder of Raquel New York, lists buildup of dead skin cells on the surface, poor barrier function that leads to chronic dehydration, or even using the wrong products as common reasons for dull skin. Board-certified dermatologist and Skin of Color Society member Shauna Higgins, MD, agrees; she adds that dehydration, sun damage, impaired skin-cell turnover, uneven skin tone, and lifestyle and environmental factors such as smoking and air pollution are other causes to consider.

articles.title: Long Live the Chaotic Step-And-Repeat!
articles.summary: There is something so delightful about seeing celebrities, glammed up and dressed in their finest fashions, thrust in front of a graphic design monstrosity.
body: Last night, a host of marquee celebrities—Charli xcx, Greta Lee, Matthew McConaughey, Serena Williams, and Charlize Theron among them—descended upon Milk Studios in Los Angeles for the inaugural Airbnb.org Gala.

Since the simple existence of an “Airbnb.org Gala” inspires confusion (the gala raised funds for emergency housing initiatives), its red carpet had to set the tone, telegraphing it as a serious event worthy of its impressive guest list. Attendees posed on a sand-colored carpet framed by tall grasses, with an oatmeal step-and-repeat subtly embossed with the organization’s name and insignia behind them. But while the event’s mission was admirable, its sheer randomness, coupled with the caliber of talent that showed out, did make me yearn for the halcyon days of the chaotic step-and-repeat.

When you turn it on, you'll likely note how bright this TV gets, which is a huge advantage QLEDs have over OLEDs.
